c.tagline: Gateway to the emerald limestone karsts of UNESCO-listed Ha Long Bay

taxi.color: green and white (Mai Linh) or turquoise (Halong Taxi)
taxi.fareNote: Stick to reputable companies like Mai Linh; use the Grab app to avoid overcharging, which is common with unmetered street taxis near the bay.

emergency.note: Fire is 114. English-speaking assistance may be limited; for serious medical issues, transfer to Hanoi is common.

avoid.reason: Beware cut-rate cruise booking scams and bait-and-switch boat operators — book Ha Long Bay cruises through reputable agents.

hood_desc: The main tourist district on the western shore of Ha Long Bay, packed with hotels, seafood restaurants, and the Sun World Ha Long Complex cable car and amusement park. The lively Ha Long Night Market draws visitors for souvenirs and street food each evening. Most bay cruises depart from the nearby international cruise port.

The older, more local half of the city across the bay from Bai Chay, home to the municipal offices, the central market, and the port. It offers a grittier, more authentic slice of daily Vietnamese life away from the resort crowds.

A man-made peninsula turned resort island connected by a causeway, home to a large marina, a water park, and many of the wooden junk boats used for overnight bay cruises. It has a resort-town feel with hotels, restaurants, and evening entertainment.
A quieter district built around the revered Cua Ong Temple, a hillside pilgrimage site dedicated to a 13th-century general. It sees more domestic pilgrims than foreign tourists and has a slower pace.
A relaxed residential and beach area near Bai Chay, with a public beach, small seafood shacks, and fewer crowds than the main tourist strip. It's popular with locals for weekend swims.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.map: no official transit app; Grab recommended
transit.note: Most visitors rely on hotel transfers, taxis, or Grab; walking along the Bai Chay and Hon Gai waterfronts is common.

train: No direct rail; nearest station is Hanoi, ~180km away
bus: Frequent buses and limousine vans from Hanoi (~2.5-3.5 hrs)
ferry: Boats and cruises depart from Tuan Chau Marina and Ha Long International Cruise Port for bay tours

airport.name: Van Don International Airport (VDO)
rentals: Limited local operators; hotel transfers common

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Vietnam, but rounding up or 5-10% for good service in tourist restaurants is appreciated; tour guides and boat crews often expect a small tip.
